title: Houthi attack on Yemeni government forces kills 53: officials
summary: Fifty-three people were killed and 200 were injured in an attack on Monday by Iran-aligned Houthi rebels on a government security forces training camp in ‌Yemen's coastal Shabwa province, according…

image.caption: This file photo shows members of the Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces as they patrol a road in Taiz province on Sept. 30. Dozens of Yemeni forces were killed in a Houthi attack on a training camp in Shabwa province on Monday. (Ebrahim Al-Suhaibi/Reuters)

blocks.text: Fifty-three people were killed and 200 were injured in an attack on Monday by Iran-aligned Houthi rebels on a government security forces training camp in ‌Yemen's coastal Shabwa province, according to the local authority.
Fighting intesifies as Iran-backed rebels fire ballistic missiles during training exercise

Fifty-three people were killed and 200 were injured in an attack on Monday by the Iran-aligned Houthis on a government security forces training camp in ‌Yemen's Shabwa province, according to the local authority, as fighting in the country intensifies.
Video verified by Reuters from Shabwa province showed injured people and bloodied bodies scattered across the ground.

The ​Houthis and the internationally recognized government, which is ​backed by a Saudi-led coalition, have been trading attacks since the group advanced in September toward territory near the Bab ​el-Mandeb Strait, a shipping chokepoint at the mouth of the ⁠Red Sea.
Local authority ⁠sources who spoke on condition of ‌anonymity said the Houthis had launched three ballistic missiles at security forces during a training exercise.
How the Houthi-Saudi Arabia conflict plays into broader Middle East war
Shabwa, an energy-rich province in southcentral coastal Yemen overlooking the Gulf of Aden, is home to the ⁠Balhaf liquefied natural gas facility, Yemen's largest industrial investment.

Government forces this month began a campaign aimed at recapturing areas controlled by the Houthis, recovering ground near the ‌strait, while the group besieges Taiz, the last major urban stronghold of anti-Houthi forces in the southern highland area of Yemen.

The conflict in Yemen has become another frontline in the wider U.S.-Israeli ​war on Iran as the Houthis have escalated their attacks on Saudi Arabia, the world's largest ⁠crude exporter, targeting Riyadh's international airport and the state oil company Saudi Aramco.

blocks.text: War ⁠broke out in Yemen in 2014 when the Houthis seized the capital ⁠Sanaa, ⁠driving the government south. ​A Saudi-led military intervention the following year led to a bloody stalemate until the ​sides agreed a ⁠2022 truce that held until this year.
Yemen is already one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, with aid agencies warning of rapidly deteriorating conditions there.
